subject: Tenant Traceback Launchpad — instrumentation + dashboard ask
messages:
From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 9 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Tenant Traceback Launchpad — instrumentation + dashboard ask

Team —

Following the Acme demo last week, they asked for a single pane where their SREs can: 1) see a tenant-specific cost/latency breakdown, 2) jump to the exact inference trace (token-path) for a sampled request, and 3) get quick remediation suggestions (e.g., switch to cached model variant, reduce max_tokens).

Current gaps we should address in the launchpad MVP:
- Traceability: add tenant_id to the request trace header and ensure it survives across internal RPC hops (router -> inference pool -> cache).
- Token-path snapshots: store a compact token-path fingerprint (not full PII content) for sampled traces so we can reconstruct cost and latency per-token segment.
- Dashboard UX: a tenant filter, heatmap for endpoint cost, top 3 heavy callchains, and a quick "jump to trace" that opens the trace viewer with the annotated token-cost timeline.
- Retention & sampling: default 7d full-sample retention, 30d aggregated metrics; 0.5% request sampling for detailed token-paths with opt-in higher sampling for enterprise customers.

Can we align on owners and a realistic engineering scope for a canary? My propose:
- Marissa: product requirements + wireframe sign-off (I attached a rough PDF).
- Kimberly: infra feasibility (storage, indexing, query latencies) + sampling config limits.
- Jonas: analytics/alerting integration and cost-attribution mapping to billing.

Asks for today's sync: rough feasibility note + ballpark effort (S/M/L), and thumbs on the sampling/retention defaults.

Thanks,
Mateo

--
Mateo Alvarez
Senior Solutions PM | Redwood Inference
mateo_alvarez@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0192

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 9 May 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Tenant Traceback Launchpad — instrumentation + dashboard ask

+1 on the priority. Quick notes after a first pass:

- Adding tenant_id to traces is straightforward, but we need to ensure it doesn't leak into model inputs in plaintext — will add as metadata on the tracing span.
- Token-path fingerprinting: store a hashed/normalized representation (sequence of token-ids + segment boundaries) to avoid storing LLM outputs. Estimated storage: 30KB/sample before compression; with 0.5% sampling across enterprise traffic (~10k rps), that's non-trivial. We should cap detailed sampling per-customer at 50QPS.
- Indexing/query: want to prototype using our existing time-series + elastic trace index combo. Expect a 2-week spike to wire up ingestion and query endpoints for the "jump to trace" flow.

Rough effort: infra prototype (S; 2 weeks), production rollout (M; 6–8 weeks including ops hardening).

I'll follow up with a short doc on storage estimates and an ops play for canary deletion and retention policies.

Kimberly

--
Kimberly Park
Engineering Lead, Observability | Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 9 May 2027 13:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Tenant Traceback Launchpad — instrumentation + dashboard ask

Thanks — this looks doable and aligns with a lot of PM requests. A few product clarifications:

- Access control: the launchpad needs RBAC so customer SREs only see their tenant. We should use existing tenant-scoped tokens; add an admin toggle for Redwood CS to view multi-tenant rollups.
- UX priority: the "jump to trace" should preserve the query parameters (start time, endpoint, route) and show a compact timeline with cost hotspots (token buckets that consumed >X GPU-ms).
- Alerts: propose a default alert template for high-cost spikes per-tenant (threshold + sudden-percentile-shift) and a suggested remediation. Jonas, can we map alerted spike to billing tag (route id + model variant)?

Attachments: I exported a CSV of the top 10 heavy tenant queries from the Acme POC (sampled) — included for context.

I'll host a short walkthrough Monday to align on UX microcopy and the default alert thresholds.

-Marissa

--
Marissa Cole
Product Manager, Observability | Redwood Inference

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 9 May 2027 15:01:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Tenant Traceback Launchpad — instrumentation + dashboard ask

I'll take ownership of alert mapping and billing linkage. Quick answers:

- We can map spike -> billing tags by joining the trace fingerprint to the token-path cost model table (we already annotate each request with route_id and model_variant). That join should be precomputed into a daily shard for quick queries.
- For the jump-to-trace UX, we need a small API change: allow querying traces by (tenant_id, trace_fingerprint) in addition to time-window. I estimate a small schema change in traces storage (S; 3 days) and an indexing job (M; 2 weeks).
- Alert templates: I'll draft two templates (cost spike, latency tail spike) and include recommended thresholds for enterprise vs self-serve.

Putting a tentative owner list in this thread:
- PM & UX: Marissa
- Infra instrumentation + sampling: Kimberly
- Billing/analytics mapping: Jonas
- Solutions/CS pilot: Mateo

I'll post the alert templates tomorrow.

Jonas

From: Ben Harper <ben.harper@acme-analytics.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>
Cc: Acme Analytics Platform Team <platform@acme-analytics.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 9 May 2027 20:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Tenant Traceback Launchpad — instrumentation + dashboard ask

Mateo — thanks for looping us in and for the wireframe. This would be a huge help for our SREs. A couple quick asks from our side before the pilot:

1) Can the launchpad show the effective model variant and quantization level used for the sampled trace? We need that to reproduce cost deltas.
2) For privacy, ensure the token-path snapshots are redacted — we only need token-ids and timing, not model outputs.
3) Can you include a per-trace "estimated token cost" number that maps to our billing line-item? That'll speed up our runbooks.

Happy to join the Monday walkthrough. Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Ben
Platform Engineer | Acme Analytics
ben.harper@acme-analytics.com
